newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO police block Israel establishing Gaza outpost.
newsitem.headline: PLO police block Israel establishing Gaza outpost.

text.p: Palestinian police on Wednesday blocked Israeli soldiers trying to restore a military outpost in self-ruled Gaza that was dismantled some 18 months ago, PLO officers said.
The incident, which was later resolved peacefully, briefly raised tension in the area where Palestinian policemen and Israeli soldiers took fighting positions, witnesses said.

A senior PLO officer said Israeli soldiers brought mobile homes without coordinating with the Palestinian side and were trying to re-establish a radar station at the site overlooking a main road used by Palestinians.
"We were astonished when the Israeli side came with a large force trying to set up a radar station in the area of Sheikh Ijlin near the sea," said Colonel Radwan Abu al-Qumsan.
Palestinian policemen stationed near the site blocked the main intersection near the settlement of Netzarim, forcing the Israelis to take the equipment back to the settlement.
Israel's commander of the southern region, which includes the Gaza Strip, denied the attempt was intended to create a new outpost.

"We are not creating a new observation post...There is no reason why the other side should interpret (this as anything other than) routine and on-going army operations," Major-General Shlomo Yanai told Israel Radio.
Brigadier-General Saeb al-Ajez, commander of the Palestinian police in northern Gaza, said the problem was resolved.
"It was agreed that no Israeli presence should be in any part of this area," Ajez told reporters.
Palestinians said the incident raised tension in the area. More than 200 Palestinian civilians briefly gathered at the site.

Israel handed over most of the Gaza Strip to Palestinian police in 1994 under a self-rule peace deal. Israeli soldiers remained to guard a few thousand Jewish settlers living in 19 enclaves strewn across the coastal area.
The Sheikh Ijlin area, south of Gaza City, is being developed by Palestinians for recreation. Several restaurants and seaside cafes have been set up.
